scope: Theorem 1.1 (Uniform relative denominators) of the manuscript “Relative denominators and effective systems for log Calabi-Yau fibrations” (preprints/Relative-denominators-and-effective-systems-for-log-Calabi-Yau-fibrations-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 034 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 a539053eb28e6c4d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 2. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix a finite set Φ ⊂ [0, 1] ∩ Q and an integer 1 ≤ d ≤ 4. There are positive integers p0 | p, with p0 clearing Φ, and a rational DCC set B ⊂ [0, 1], depending only on d and Φ, with the following property. Suppose (X, B) is a projective lc pair of dimension d with coefficients in Φ, and f : X −→ Z, dim Z > 0, KX + B ∼Q f ∗ D, where f is a contraction and D is a rational Cartier divisor. There exist ψ ∈ C(X)∗ and DZ ∼Q D such that KX + B + 1 p0 Div(ψ) = f ∗ DZ, DZ = KZ + BZ + MZ. (1.1) Here BZ is effective with coefficients in B, the pair (Z, BZ + MZ) is generalized lc, and M is b-nef with pM b-Cartier. If (X, B) is klt, the generalized pair is generalized klt.
